headline: AKS IS INSUFFICIENT, MACHINE-CHECKED (Attack01.aks_bound_insufficient). For every r >= 1 there is an explicit f satisfying the cited AKS conclusion VinogradovLE f (scale (4*r)) and REFUTING VinogradovLE f (scale r). So no derivation consuming `alon_krivelevich_sudakov` as a black box can prove ConjectureAt r. The spec's prose claim that the exponent gap IS the open problem is now a theorem.

THE UNIVERSE IS NOT PART OF THE PROBLEM (Attack01.conjectureAt_of_fin / conjectureAt_fin_iff). Proving the bound for bipartite r-degenerate graphs on Fin m, for every m, proves ConjectureAt.{u} r in EVERY universe u; at u=0 it is an iff. A mechanised attack may work entirely with Fin-indexed graphs.

BOTH AXES MOVE STRICTLY, IN OPPOSITE DIRECTIONS. Conclusion axis (Attack01.scale_not_vinogradov): scale s is never << scale r for r < s. Hypothesis axis (Attack02.degeneracy_hierarchy_strict): K_{r,r} is bipartite, r-degenerate, and NOT k-degenerate for any k < r. More graphs, weaker bound - so no ConjectureAt k implies any other, and r=2 is genuinely its own problem.

A DEGENERACY ORDER EXISTS (Attack01.exists_degeneracyList). Every finite r-degenerate graph has a vertex list in which each vertex has at most r neighbours among those still to come. Read backwards this is the greedy-embedding order - the input the r=1 proof needs.
open: ConjectureAt 2 (Conjecture_r_two) - UNTOUCHED. Nothing in this campaign bears on its truth.
Conjecture, ConjectureAt r for r >= 1 - UNTOUCHED.

ConjectureAt 1 - NOT PROVED, though the target is now visible. Two lemmas are missing and neither was attempted: (a) MIN-DEGREE EXTRACTION - a finite graph G with #E(G) > k * #V(G) has a nonempty vertex subset whose induced subgraph has minimum degree > k (proved by repeatedly deleting a vertex of degree <= k; the invariant e > k*v survives each deletion, and forces nonemptiness at the end); (b) GREEDY EMBEDDING - given the degeneracy order of Attack01.exists_degeneracyList for a 1-degenerate H on h vertices and a graph G of minimum degree >= h, build a SimpleGraph.Copy H G by placing vertices in reverse list order, each attaching to at most 1 already-placed vertex. (b) is the expensive half: it constructs a term of Copy by induction along a list and is a multi-hundred-line development, not a budget-8 job.
The spec's convention (1) counterexample (P4 vs K_{n/2,n/2}, showing the INDUCED reading of the conjecture is false) - not formalized. It needs a lower bound on an induced-Turan number.

The spec's convention (9) claim (a single Vinogradov constant working for all H at once is false) - not formalized. It needs Kovari-Sos-Turan-type LOWER bounds on ex(n; K_{r,r}), which this campaign has no machinery for.

obstructionMap.conclusionAxis: CLOSED as an obstruction. scale is strictly increasing in r under <<; proved via rpow_not_vinogradov, whose engine is Tendsto (n ^ (a-b)) atTop atTop for a > b. Any future attempt to reach ConjectureAt r from a weaker exponent is refuted at the level of the bound itself, before any graph theory.
obstructionMap.hypothesisAxis: CLOSED as an obstruction. K_{r,r} witnesses strictness of IsDegenerate inside the bipartite class.
obstructionMap.reductionAxis: PARTIALLY OPEN. Universe quantifier eliminated (conjectureAt_of_fin). Edge-maximality reduction available (vinogradov_of_isContained + IsDegenerate.of_isContained). The r=0 conjunct proved free (conjectureAt_zero, conjecture_iff_ge_one). What remains unreduced is the quantifier over m and over graphs on Fin m.
obstructionMap.constructiveAxis: OPEN. This is where the remaining work is: min-degree extraction and greedy embedding (see `open` above). Nothing in this campaign produces an upper bound on ex(n;H) better than the trivial n^2 (Attack01.exR_vinogradov_sq), and Attack01.distance_to_target proves that trivial bound is strictly insufficient. The entire content of the target lies in that gap, and the gap is untouched.
